planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun with room to spread; strong light keeps the burgundy-black foliage from fading toward green.

directions: Summer Wine Rosé pairs the dark burgundy-black foliage familiar from earlier Summer Wine selections with very pale pink spring flower clusters, a softer bloom tone than the white-flowered originals in the series. Its full-size, upright habit needs generous spacing and open airflow to avoid foliar mildew in humid summers, and the foliage holds its darkest color with a full day of direct sun. Established plants tolerate clay, periodic wet soil, and urban growing conditions typical of native ninebark. Renewal-prune by removing the oldest stems near the base every couple of years rather than shearing the whole plant.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil; full sun to part shade sustains the heaviest, most colorfast bloom on this compact mound.

directions: Happy Face Orange brings a true creamsicle-orange flower color to the shrubby cinquefoil group, a shade the breeder markets as holding steady through summer heat rather than fading toward yellow or pink like many older orange-toned selections. Small five-petaled flowers cover the mounded, fine-textured shrub in heavy flushes from late spring into fall. Once established it tolerates drought, poor soil, and harsh winters with little complaint, making it a reliable low shrub for cold-climate borders. Little pruning is needed beyond an occasional thinning cut to keep the habit tidy.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained soil; a full day of direct sun deepens the reddish-pink flower color and keeps the upright habit dense.

directions: Paraplu Red extends the flat-opening, umbrella-shaped bloom form of the Paraplu rose-of-sharon line into a deep reddish-pink color, with the shade intensifying in partial shade and softening in full sun. Flowers open continuously on new wood through summer into fall on an upright, late-leafing shrub, giving months of color without deadheading. It draws bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds while resisting deer browsing and tolerating short dry spells once rooted in. A light shaping cut in late winter is the only routine care it needs.

planting.note: Plant container vines in spring against a trellis or fence in well-drained soil; full sun to part shade keeps the showy bracts fullest.

directions: Kintzley's Ghost is a non-invasive native honeysuckle vine grown as much for its large, rounded bracts as for its yellow summer flowers, with the dusty blue-green bracts persisting well after bloom and resembling eucalyptus foliage. Red berries follow in fall, adding a second season of interest and drawing songbirds. It climbs by twining and benefits from a trellis, arbor, or fence to support its reach, tolerating drought and deer pressure once established. Little pruning is required beyond removing dead or crossing stems in late winter.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in spring in well-drained soil; space for good air circulation to support continuous rebloom without deadheading.

directions: Oso Easy Red Stripe stands out from earlier solid-color Oso Easy selections with hot pink-red petals striped in cream, giving every bloom a painted, variegated look. Flowers open continuously on new growth through summer without deadheading, backed by dark green, disease-resistant foliage on a vigorous upright shrub. It carries light fragrance along with the series' usual toughness against black spot and powdery mildew. Cut the plant back by about a third in early spring to keep it full and encourage strong new flowering canes.
